culture.name: Mexico
culture.timeDifference: It is about the same time there, give or take an hour or two.
culture.homeTravelNote: a flight of a few hours, close enough that home feels within reach

cookLines: Dried chiles toast in the pan and the whole apartment smells like home.
You taste the mole and stir in a little more chocolate, the way your grandmother would.
{roommate} wanders in and asks what smells so good.
You share warm tortillas at the counter, and for an hour the world is small and warm.

festivals.title: El Grito, far from home
festivals.body: On the night of 15 September, people at home gather to shout "¡Viva México!" for Independence Day on the 16th. Here it is a regular school night.
festivals.join: Go to the student association's Grito party.
festivals.joinText: Green, white and red streamers, pozole in paper bowls and a room full of people shouting together. You lose your voice and do not mind.
festivals.host: Invite friends over for pozole and the Grito on a laptop.
festivals.hostText: Your friends learn to shout "¡Viva!" on cue. Someone's cousin sends a video from the Zócalo at the perfect moment.
festivals.skip: Watch the Grito on your phone between assignments.
festivals.skipText: The bells ring from the screen while you finish a problem set. You whisper along anyway.

festivals.title: Día de Muertos
festivals.body: At home your family is setting up the ofrenda with marigolds, candles and photos of the people you miss. Here, the first week of November is midterm season.
festivals.join: Help with the community ofrenda at the student center.
festivals.joinText: You place a photo of your grandfather next to dozens of others. Strangers ask about him, and you tell them.
festivals.host: Build a small ofrenda in your room and invite friends.
festivals.hostText: A shelf becomes an altar with paper flowers and pan de muerto from the bakery. Your friends bring photos of their own people.
festivals.skip: Light one candle and call home.
festivals.skipText: Your mother turns the phone toward the altar so you can see every face. It is enough for tonight.

festivals.title: Nochebuena
festivals.body: At home, Christmas Eve means a late dinner, tamales, family everywhere and someone falling asleep before midnight. The dorms are emptying out for the break.
festivals.join: Go to a friend's family dinner across town.
festivals.joinText: Their tía hands you a plate before you take off your coat. You stay past midnight.
festivals.host: Make tamales with whoever is still on campus.
festivals.hostText: The kitchen turns into an assembly line of husks and masa. Half the tamales fall apart and everyone eats them anyway.
festivals.skip: Video-call the family dinner and go to bed early.
festivals.skipText: Your little cousins pass the phone around the table. You fall asleep to the sound of home.

familyCall: It is barely an hour's difference, so your mother calls while she is making lunch.
She tilts the phone toward the stove so you can see the pot of beans.
Your little cousin grabs the phone to show you a drawing, and your grandmother asks when you are coming home.
You hang up hungry and homesick, and a little lighter.
culture.homeMoneyNote: Money from home is converted from pesos, and every swing in the exchange rate shows up in your account.
culture.familySupportNote: Kept at the India baseline. The research has no sourced figure that would justify more or less family support for Mexican students; money still moves through peso exchange rates much as it does through rupees. Cheaper flights home are handled by roundTripFlightUsd, not by this factor.

entryNotes.F1: Mexico is not among the top five F-1 source countries; some graduates later move from F-1 to TN status.
entryNotes.H1B: Many Mexican professionals use the TN visa instead, which has no lottery; Mexicans received 15,630 of 15,672 TN visas in FY2024.
entryNotes.B2: Mexicans can apply for a Border Crossing Card, a ten-year visitor card; about 1.87 million were issued in FY2024.
entryNotes.O1: Mexican nationals received 880 O-1 visas in FY2024.
entryNotes.FAM: Family preference waits for Mexico are among the longest; in the November 2026 bulletin, sibling petitions from before April 2001 are being processed.
entryNotes.EWI: Mexican nationals were 47 percent of Border Patrol southwest apprehensions in FY2025, and entering without inspection usually blocks a green card from inside the US later.
entryNotes.ASY: In FY2024 immigration courts granted about 16 percent of decided asylum cases from Mexican applicants.

facts.title: Time difference to Mexico City
facts.text: Mexico City is on UTC-6 all year and no longer uses daylight saving time. It is 1 hour behind US Eastern in winter and 2 hours behind in summer, level with US Central in winter, and 1 to 2 hours ahead of Pacific.

facts.title: Round-trip flight, Mexico to US
facts.text: Design estimate of $450. No sourced fare range for Mexico to US round trips was found in the research; real fares vary widely by route and season.

facts.title: Remittances to Mexico
facts.text: Mexico received $61.79 billion in remittances in 2025, down 4.6 percent from $64.7 billion in 2024, the biggest fall since 2009 (Banxico, as reported).

facts.title: Mexico and the TN visa
facts.text: Mexico's share of H-1B approvals was not found in the research. The main professional route is the TN visa: Mexicans received 15,630 of 15,672 TN visas in FY2024 (99.7 percent).

facts.title: Asylum decisions for Mexican applicants
facts.text: In FY2024 immigration courts granted 751 and denied 3,910 asylum cases from Mexican nationals, about 16 percent of decisions. Another 12,775 were not adjudicated. Individual claims matter more than averages.

facts.title: Family green card queue for Mexico
facts.text: November 2026 Visa Bulletin final action dates for Mexico, as transcribed by law firms: adult children of citizens (F1) 22 Sep 2008, married children (F3) 15 Jul 2001, siblings (F4) 22 Apr 2001. A sibling petition filed today faces a wait of roughly 25 years.

mechanics.asylumNote: 751 grants and 3,910 denials in FY2024, about 16 percent; the game has used 18 (research/unauthorized-entry.md 2.5).
